items.actClause:
AN ACT to amend the village law and the public officers law, in relation to
permitting building inspectors, fire inspectors and code enforcement officers
of the village of Buchanan, county of Westchester, to live within Westchester
county, an adjoining county or Dutchess county
items.lawCode: Amd §3-300, Vil L; amd §3, Pub Off L
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S6654

SPONSOR: HARCKHAM
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the village law and the public officers law, in relation
to permitting building inspectors, fire inspectors and code enforcement
officers of the village of Buchanan, county of Westchester, to live
within Westchester county, an adjoining county or Dutchess county

 
PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA OF BILL:

This legislation would allow building inspectors, fire inspectors ad .
code enforcement officers in the village of Buchanan to be residents of
Westchester County or an adjoining county.

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section 1. The Village of Buchanan has employed individuals that reside
outside of the political subdivision or municipal corporation in
violation of the Public Officers Law and Village Law. Notwithstanding
this defect, their employment was validated, legalized, ratified and
confirmed, notwithstanding the absence of prior legislative approval.

Section 2. A new subdivision 31 is added to Section 3-300 of the Village
Law stating that by resolution, the Village of Buchanan may provide that
the office of building inspector, fire inspector and code enforcement
officers need not be a resident of such village but may be a person who
is not a resident of Buchanan as long as they are a resident of West-
chester County or an adjoining county but is a resident of Westchester
County or an adjoining county within New York State.

Section 3. A new subdivision 71 is added to Section 3 of the Public
Officers Law stating: In the Village of Buchanan, the provisions of this
section requiring a person to be a resident of the political subdivision
or municipal corporation of the state for which he or she shall be
chosen or within which his or her official functions are required to be
exercised, shall not prevent a person from holding the office of build-
ing inspector, fire inspector and code enforcement officers of such
village, provided that the person performing the functions of building
inspector, fire inspector and code enforcement officers in any other
village shall reside in Westchester county or an adjoining county of the
State of New York; provided, however that the person performing the
functions of building inspector, fire inspector and code enforcement
officers in any other village shall be a resident of such village unless
otherwise provided by law.

Section 4. This act shall take effect immediately.

 
DIFFERENCE BETWEEN ORIGINAL AND AMENDED VERSION (IF APPLICABLE):

This portion of this memorandum is not applicable at this time.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

While the Building Inspector and Assistant Building Inspector for the
Village of Buchanan were in the process of being appointed, and current-
ly serving during a probationary period, the Department of Human
Resources of Westchester County concluded that the persons performing
these functions are subject to the residency requirements of the Public
Officers Law. This means that at the very least, these inspectors must
be residents of New York State as well as residents of the Village of
Buchanan, which they are not. Therefore, the Village of Buchanan is
requesting that this legislation be introduced to expand the residency
requirements for their building inspectors, fire inspectors and code
enforcement officers.

By allowing a non-resident of the Village of Buchanan, as long as they
are a resident of Westchester County, an adjoining county within the
state of New York, to hold the position of building inspector, fire
inspector and/or code enforcement inspector, there is more of an oppor-
tunity to recruit and retain qualified candidates. Currently, candidates
are not allowed to live outside of the village of Buchanan.

 
PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

This is new legislation.

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS FOR STATE AND LOCAL GOVERNMENTS:

There are no fiscal implications to the State or local government in
association with the passage of this legislation.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect immediately.
